question: Can the SLL pass resolve the valid constructs that currently force a full-file LL fallback, without changing diagnostics or parse trees?
hypothesis: Two SLL prediction conflicts account for most production fallbacks. Resolving collection-method dotted access with full-context prediction and skipping the select-list alias before BULK COLLECT will remove those fallbacks while keeping every parse tree, token count, and diagnostic unchanged.
control: experiments/006-routine-name-and-general-element/report.json; paired fresh control was generated with LAB_GENERATED_OPTIMIZATIONS=generalElement,generalElementPart,routineName
candidate: Default generated parser with generalElement, collectionMethodCall, generalElementPart, bulkCollectAlias, and routineName optimizations

command.conformance: LAB_TREE_HASH=1 node grammar/typescript/harness.ts for the control and candidate generated states

selection: Complete frozen 1,244-file opaque production corpus; tail statistics reuse the 12 opaque ids selected by experiment 004.

classification.rootCause: Diagnostics were attributed to the parser rule that reported them; cascaded diagnostics were grouped under the first error in each file.
classification.collectionMethodCall: 66 files first failed at a collection method such as aTableData.EXTEND, because DELETE, EXTEND, and TRIM are valid regular_id tokens and SLL continued general_element through the period.
classification.bulkCollectInto: 49 files first failed at COLLECT because SLL consumed BULK as a select-list alias; LL resolves the conflict from the following COLLECT.
classification.remaining: 14 of the remaining 20 files are genuine grammar gaps that also fail under LL; 6 are additional SLL-only conflicts not addressed by this change.

acceptance: Full-file LL fallback count or LL elapsed time decreases repeatably on production evidence.
Total parser-core time improves without material SLL regression on files that already parsed under SLL.
Diagnostics remain explicit and parse-tree digests, token counts, lexer diagnostics, and parser diagnostics are unchanged.
Focused tests cover malformed collection methods, malformed BULK COLLECT, and unsupported XMLTABLE and DATE NULL syntax.
Results include repeated full-corpus and tail-set measurements.
Only opaque file identities, hashes, and aggregate evidence leave the private corpus.
limitations: The 12-file tail is inherited from experiment 004 and is deliberately biased to the highest-cost files.
Three repetitions give a descriptive deterministic bootstrap interval, not a production guarantee; one tail control campaign was excluded for host slowdown and retained in measurements.json.
Six SLL-only conflicts remain; they are not classified as grammar gaps because LL accepts the same source.
The local full-context predictions are coupled to generated decision numbers and pinned antlr-ng output.
The laboratory has no production semantic indexer; identical parse-tree digests and diagnostics are the semantic-consumer boundary.
Java is an unmodified control and does not include the TypeScript generated-code optimization.
